title: Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea
title_original: 국립해양생물자원관의 설립 및 운영에 관한 법률
full_text:
ACT ON THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF THE NATIONAL MARINE BIODIVERSITY INSTITUTE OF KOREA

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to establish the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea, thereby conserving marine biological resources and contributing to the development of the marine and fisheries industries through the systematic collection, preservation, exhibition, research, and other activities concerning marine biological resources. <Amended Apr. 18, 2017>

Article 2 (Legal Personality)
The National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea (hereinafter referred to as the "Institute") shall be a legal entity.

Article 3 (Establishment)
① The Institute shall be established upon registration of its incorporation at the location of its principal office.
② The matters to be registered for incorporation under paragraph ① shall be as follows:
1. Purpose;
2. Name;
3. Principal office and affiliated institutions;
4. Names and addresses of its executive officers;
5. Method of giving public notice.
③ Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to registration of the Institute.

Article 4 (Articles of Incorporation)
① The articles of incorporation of the Institute shall include the following matters:
1. Purpose;
2. Name;
3. Location of its principal office;
4. Its affairs and the execution thereof;
5. Property and accounting;
6. Organization and affiliated institutions;
7. Executive officers and employees;
8. Board of directors;
9. Amendments to the articles of incorporation;
10. Method of giving public notice.
② An amendment to the articles of incorporation of the Institute shall be resolved upon by the board of directors with the consent of at least two-thirds of the incumbent directors and shall obtain authorization from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 5 (Business)
① The Institute shall conduct the following business:
1. Collection, preservation, management, and exhibition of marine biological resources;
2. Surveys and research concerning marine biological resources;
3. Education concerning marine biological resources;
4. Domestic and international exchanges and cooperation relating to marine biological resources;
5. Collection, acceptance on entrustment, registration, preservation, management, utilization, and evaluation of information derived from marine biological resources;
6. Revenue-generating business to procure operating funds within the scope of the purposes for which the Institute is established;
7. Affairs incidental to the business referred to in subparagraphs 1 through 6;
8. Other affairs relating to marine biological resources entrusted to the Institute by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
② To conduct revenue-generating business under paragraph ① 6, the Institute shall obtain approval from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries for each such business.

Article 6 (Executive Officers)
① The Institute shall have one Director, one executive director, not more than five non-executive directors, and one auditor as its executive officers.
② The auditor shall serve on a non-executive basis.
③ The Director shall be appointed and dismissed by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries as prescribed by the articles of incorporation. The appointment and dismissal of the executive director, non-executive directors, and auditor shall be governed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 7 (Terms of Office of Executive Officers)
① The term of office of the Director shall be three years, and the Director may be reappointed for successive one-year terms.
② The term of office of a director or auditor shall be two years, and such officer may be reappointed for successive one-year terms.
③ The term of office of an executive officer appointed due to the resignation of an executive officer or for any other reason shall commence anew.

Article 8 (Duties of Executive Officers)
① The Director shall represent the Institute, exercise overall control over its affairs, and direct and supervise its employees.
② If the Director is unable to perform the duties of the office due to unavoidable circumstances, the executive director shall act on behalf of the Director. If the executive director is also unable to perform such duties, an executive officer designated by the articles of incorporation shall act on behalf of the Director.
③ Directors shall attend meetings of the board of directors and deliberate on matters submitted to the board.
④ The auditor shall audit the Institute's accounting and the execution of its affairs.

Article 9 (Disqualifications for Executive Officers)
① None of the following persons may become an executive officer of the Institute:
1. A person falling under any subparagraph of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act;
2. A person for whom three years have not elapsed since dismissal under Article 22 (1), Article 35 (2) or (3), Article 36 (2), or Article 48 (4) or (8) of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions.
② If an executive officer comes to fall under any subparagraph of paragraph ① or is found to have fallen under any such subparagraph at the time of appointment, the executive officer shall retire from office as a matter of law.
③ An act in which an executive officer who retires under paragraph ② was involved before retirement shall remain valid.

Article 10 (Board of Directors)
① The Institute shall establish a board of directors to deliberate and resolve important matters concerning the Institute.
② The board of directors shall consist of directors, including its chairperson.
③ The Director shall serve as chairperson of the board of directors. If the chairperson is unable to perform the duties of the office due to unavoidable circumstances, the executive director shall act on behalf of the chairperson. If the executive director is also unable to perform such duties, a person elected from among the non-executive directors shall act on behalf of the chairperson.
④ The chairperson may convene a meeting of the board of directors when the chairperson deems it necessary; provided, the chairperson shall convene a meeting if at least one-third of the incumbent directors so request, or if the auditor so requests in order to report the results of an audit concerning an unlawful or improper matter.
⑤ Resolutions of the board of directors shall be adopted with the consent of a majority of the incumbent directors.
⑥ The auditor may attend and speak at meetings of the board of directors when necessary in connection with the auditor's duties.

Article 11 (Sources of Funds)
① Expenses necessary for the business and operation of the Institute shall be met from the following sources:
1. Contributions, subsidies, and donations from the State or persons other than the State;
2. Borrowings under Article 13;
3. Revenue generated from the operation of the Institute;
4. Other income.
② The State may make contributions or grant subsidies to cover expenses necessary for the business and operation of the Institute within the scope of its budget.
③ An individual, corporation, or organization may contribute or donate money or other property to the Institute to support the performance of its affairs.
④ Matters necessary for the procedures for accepting donated money and goods under paragraph ③ shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 12 (Fiscal Years, Business Plans, etc.)
① The fiscal year of the Institute shall coincide with the fiscal year of the Government.
② As prescribed by Presidential Decree, the Director shall prepare and submit a business plan and budget and obtain approval thereof from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries before the commencement of each fiscal year. The same shall apply to any amendment thereto.
③ As prescribed by Presidential Decree, within two months after the end of each fiscal year, the Director shall report to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries a report stating the business performance for that fiscal year and statements of settlement of revenue and expenditure that have been audited by a certified public accountant (including an accounting corporation under Article 23 of the Certified Public Accountant Act) and resolved upon by the board of directors.

Article 13 (Borrowings)
If necessary for its operation, the Institute may borrow funds on a long-term basis with the approval of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 14 (Requests for Provision of Materials)
The Director may request relevant administrative agencies, educational institutions, research organizations, or other relevant persons to permit inspection, copying, or lending of materials relating to marine biological resources or to arrange exhibitions of such materials on entrustment.

Article 15 (Requests for Dispatch of Public Officials, etc.)
① If particularly necessary to perform the Institute's affairs, the Director may request the heads of relevant administrative agencies or research institutes to dispatch public officials or other personnel under their jurisdiction, with the approval of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
② The heads of relevant administrative agencies or research institutes receiving a request under paragraph ① may dispatch personnel under their jurisdiction to the Institute.

Article 16 (Supervision)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall guide and supervise the Institute and may make recommendations or issue orders concerning its business when deemed necessary.
② The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall conduct an evaluation of the operation of the Institute in accordance with the standards and procedures prescribed by Presidential Decree and shall formulate necessary measures based on the results thereof.
③ The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may require the Institute to submit reports on its affairs, accounting, and property, or inspect such matters, when deemed necessary.

Article 17 (Duty to Maintain Confidentiality)
No current or former executive officer or employee of the Institute shall disclose or misappropriate any confidential information learned in the course of performing their duties.

Article 18 (Prohibition on Use of Similar Names)
No person or entity other than the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea established under this Act shall use the name "National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea" or any similar name.

Article 19 (Cooperative Projects)
The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may undertake cooperative projects at the request of the local government having jurisdiction over the location of the Institute's principal office.

Article 20 (Application Mutatis Mutandis)
Except as provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Institute.

Article 21 (Deeming Executive Officers and Employees to Be Public Officials for Application of Penal Provisions)
Executive officers and employees of the Institute shall be deemed public officials for the purposes of applying Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

Article 22 (Penalty Provisions)
Any person who violates Article 17 by disclosing or misappropriating confidential information learned in the course of performing their duties shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won.

Article 23 (Administrative Fines)
① Any person who uses the name "National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea" or any similar name in violation of Article 18 shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won.
② Administrative fines under paragraph ① shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 12819, Oct. 15, 2014>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date six months after its promulgation; provided, Articles 2 and 7 of these Addenda shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

Article 2 (Preparation for Establishment)
① Within two months from the date of promulgation of this Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall establish the Establishment Committee for the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea (hereinafter referred to as the "Establishment Committee"), consisting of not more than five establishment committee members, to take charge of affairs concerning establishment of the Institute and the selection of directors and an auditor at the time of its establishment. In such case, the chairperson and members shall be appointed or commissioned by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
② The Establishment Committee shall prepare the articles of incorporation of the Institute and obtain authorization therefor from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
③ The Director of the Institute at the time of its establishment shall be appointed by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
④ Upon obtaining authorization under paragraph ②, the Establishment Committee shall, without delay, jointly sign and complete registration of the establishment of the Institute and then transfer its affairs to the Director.
⑤ When the transfer of affairs under paragraph ④ has been completed, the Establishment Committee shall be deemed dissolved and its members shall be deemed released from their commissions.
⑥ Until the Institute is established, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall bear the expenses incurred in establishing the Institute.

[Enforcement Date: Oct. 15, 2014] Article 2

Article 3 (Transfer of Goods Without Compensation)
Notwithstanding the Goods Management Act, the State may transfer without compensation to the Institute goods owned by the State and managed, as at the time this Act enters into force, by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (limited to the Planning Group for the Establishment of the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea). In such case, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall seek the Director's opinion as to the necessity of the goods and consult in advance with the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 4 (Succession to Rights and Obligations)
The Institute established under this Act shall comprehensively succeed to the rights and obligations belonging to the Planning Group for the Establishment of the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea at the time this Act enters into force, including rights and obligations relating to the management and operation of facilities and the collection of marine biological resources.

Article 5 (Budget at the Time of Establishment)
① Until the budget of the Institute established under this Act is finalized at the time of its establishment, the Institute may execute the budget formerly under the jurisdiction of the Planning Group for the Establishment of the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea in accordance with the previous practice.
② Expenses executed under paragraph ① shall be deemed to have been executed under the Institute's established budget once that budget has been established.

Article 6 (Special Cases concerning Appointment of Employees)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall classify public officials under the Minister's jurisdiction who were engaged in affairs concerning establishment of the Institute at the time this Act enters into force, according to their wishes, into persons who wish to be appointed employees of the Institute as a legal entity and persons who do not.
② Persons who wish to be appointed employees of the Institute under paragraph ① shall be deemed to have retired from public service and to have been appointed employees of the Institute when the legal entity is established.
③ Matters necessary for the affiliation, guarantee of status, conditions of service, and other matters concerning public officials who do not wish to be appointed employees of the Institute under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
④ The retirement age of a person who retires from public service and is appointed an employee of the Institute under paragraph ② shall be the retirement age under the State Public Officials Act applicable to the grade held by that person at the time of retirement from public service; provided, if the retirement age for employees of the Institute is higher than the retirement age under the State Public Officials Act, the retirement age for employees of the Institute shall apply.

Article 7 (Transitional Measures concerning Preparation of Budgets)
The Establishment Committee may prepare the budget of the Institute for the first fiscal year commencing after establishment of the Institute.

[Enforcement Date: Oct. 15, 2014] Article 7

ADDENDA (Framework Act on Marine and Fisheries Development) <Act No. 14804, Apr. 18, 2017>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date six months after its promulgation.

Article 2 (Amendments to Other Acts)
① Omitted.
② Part of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Marine Biodiversity Institute of Korea shall be amended as follows:

In Article 1, "marine industry" shall be replaced with "marine and fisheries industry".

③ through ⑨ Omitted.
